title: Agents report their state to decade over its socket
body:
decade has no idea whether an agent is running in a pane or what it is doing. herdr, which Jack used before, detects agents by watching panes. Jack wants decade to define its own small protocol instead, with coax as its first implementer, and no work to support harnesses or agent clients decade does not build.

## Proposal

- A new verb on the decade socket (`docs/protocol.md`) lets a client report the state of the agent in its pane: attention, done, working or idle.
- none is not reported. decade infers it for a pane whose agent never reported or whose client has gone.
- A workspace shows its most urgent pane: attention, then done, then working, then idle, then none.
- A reported state stays until it is cleared explicitly, by whatever raised it or by Jack. In the normal case the agent clears it through coax, which tells decade. Focusing a pane clears nothing.
- When a pane reaches attention while Jack is in another window, decade raises a desktop notification.
- decade builds its side. coax's side is out of scope here, and the two are tested together when Jack works on coax.

## Cost

A new verb is a protocol change, and it is part of decade-channel's API, so both crates' versions move at the next release under CLAUDE.md.

## Open

- How Jack clears a state by hand: from the sidebar, the top bar, or the pane.
- Whether a report can carry a short message, shown in the sidebar.
close_reason: Landed in c1acc26, shown by the frame in 50d4fec. Jack clears a state by clicking its mark in the sidebar. coax's side is untested until Jack works on coax.
